DirSymlinkExclusions.doc: Array with the name of the folders you don't want Nucleus Co-op to symlink, only the folders placed here get hardcopied not the files.

FileSymlinkExclusions.doc: Array with the name of the files you don't want Nucleus Co-op to symlink, useful if you want to replace files or add external files.
FileSymlinkExclusions.practice: File names Nucleus leaves out when it links the game into each instance folder, so the instance gets no file of that name from the game (one Nucleus or the handler puts there instead, such as a Steam emulator's DLL). Steam games' handlers usually list `steam_api64.dll` (or `steam_api.dll`) and `steam_appid.txt`, for Goldberg's own copies.

FileSymlinkCopyInstead.doc: Array with the name of the files you want Nucleus Co-op to make full copies of, in some cases games need certain files to be full copies or they won't run.
FileSymlinkCopyInstead.practice: Files Nucleus copies into each instance folder instead of linking them, so an instance can change its own copy (or the game refuses a linked file). Unity games are the usual case: their handlers copy `UnityPlayer.dll`, `globalgamemanagers` or `UnityCrashHandler64.exe`.

DirSymlinkCopyInstead.doc: Copy (not symlink) all files within a given folder | Folder name is relative from root game folder.

DirExclusions.doc: Folders (+ all its contents) listed here will not be linked or copied over to Nucleus game content folder, the instance folders.

KeepSymLinkOnExit.doc: Enable or disable symlink files from being deleted when Nucleus is closed | default: false.

HandlerInterval.doc: The interval in milliseconds the Handler should be updated at. Set it to 0 to disable updating (will lose all functionality that depends on ticks).
HandlerInterval.practice: Nucleus starts an update loop with this interval in milliseconds: each tick it updates and refreshes the game windows (positions, sizes, focus). 0 starts no loop at all. Almost always 100; 500 for games that don't like their windows being touched that often, mostly Unreal Engine games.

SymlinkExe.doc: If SymlinkGame is enabled, if we should copy or symlink the game executable.
SymlinkExe.practice: With `Game.SymlinkGame`, false (the default) copies the game's executable into each instance folder instead of linking it, and also a `Game.LauncherExe` given as a relative path; everything else is linked. A copy lets each instance be patched or renamed on its own, which is why handlers practically always keep it false.

SymlinkGame.doc: If we should symbolic link the game's files to a temporary directory (Nucleus instances folders in its content folder). If not will launch straight from the installation directory.

HardcopyGame.doc: Instead of Symlinking, create hard copies of the games files (copy/paste) | Be careful of storage, takes a LONG time to start a game when copying.

SupportsKeyboard.practice: Lets one player use the ordinary keyboard and mouse (the one Windows already uses), which the setup screen then offers. It's the single-keyboard option, for controller games where one player may use the keyboard; handlers rarely combine it with `Game.SupportsMultipleKeyboardsAndMice`.

KeyboardPlayerFirst.doc: If the keyboard player should be processed first.

ExecutableContext.doc: Array with the name of other files found in the executable's folder (so we don't confuse different games with similar file names). Example: Borderlands and Tales of the Borderlands share their executable name (borderlands.exe). We include 1 folder and a file that's unique to Borderlands to make sure the application doesn't confuse itself.
ExecutableContext.byEngine: By engine: rarer in Unreal Engine games.
ExecutableContext.practice: Files or folders that must exist next to the game's executable (paths relative to its folder) for this handler to match it, when the player adds a game or Nucleus searches the disks. It tells apart games that share an executable name (hl2.exe, game.exe): authors pick a file or folder only that game has, such as a DLL it ships (`binkw32.dll` is a common one) or its data folder.

MaxPlayers.practice: Only shown in the game list ("2-4" under the game's name, HorizontalGameControl); Nucleus doesn't stop anyone from assigning more players. Authors put the number of players the game handles, usually 4 or 8; Source games' handlers often say 16.

MaxPlayersOneMonitor.practice: Nothing in Nucleus reads it besides the interface that declares it: it's information for the reader of the handler. Authors usually say 4, sometimes 8 or 16.

source.what: no other use in the source

PauseBetweenStarts.doc: How long Nucleus waits before starting the next instance, in **seconds** (the official docs say milliseconds, but every place Nucleus uses it waits `TimeSpan.FromSeconds(...)`). 0 or unset: no wait. A profile's "instances startup wait time" (also seconds) replaces it. `Game.PromptBetweenInstances` still needs it.
PauseBetweenStarts.practice: Nucleus sleeps this many seconds after starting an instance, before the next one. A player can override it in the game's profile settings (Pause between instances launch); when that is above 0 it replaces the handler's value. Usually 20 to 30 seconds: enough for the game to open its window before the next copy starts; less for games that start quickly.

DPIHandling.doc: The way the games handles DPI scaling. Modify this if the game is presenting different sizing behaviour after the Windows 10 Creators Update. Values: True: True tries to send the correct width and height to the game's window. Nucleus.DPIHandling.Scaled: Scaled will scale the width and height by the DPI of the system (see that it's not per-monitor). Nucleus.DPIHandling.InvScaled: InvScaled will scale the width and height by 1 / DPI of the system (see that it's not per-monitor).

StartArguments.doc: Adds whatever you put into the field as starting parameters for the game's executable. For example, in most cases '-windowed' will force windowed mode. Parameters can be chained. Necessary for some games.

BinariesFolder.byEngine: By engine: more common in Unreal Engine games, rarer in Unity and Source games.
BinariesFolder.practice: Where the executable sits inside the game folder ("bin", "Binaries\\Win64"). Nucleus takes it off the executable's folder to find the game's root, so the whole game is linked into each instance, not only the executable's folder. Mostly Unreal Engine games' handlers set it, nearly all of them: to the project's "Binaries\\Win64" (or "Binaries\\Win32"), older Unreal games' to "System"; other games use "bin" or leave it empty.

KillMutex.doc: Array of mutexes to kill before starting the next game process. A 'Mutex/Mutant' is a mutually exclusive flag, which basically tells the game not to allow multiple instances of its program.
KillMutex.byEngine: By engine: more common in Source games, rarer in Unity games.
KillMutex.practice: Before it starts the second and later instances, Nucleus closes these named handles in the instance before (mutexes by default; `Game.KillMutexType` picks events, semaphores or sections), because many games refuse to start while another copy holds one. `Game.RenameNotKillMutex` renames them at startup instead. Find the names with a tool such as Process Explorer while the game runs. Source games share `hl2_singleton_mutex` and some Unreal Engine 4 games `UnrealEngine4`; Unity games rarely need it.

LauncherExe.doc: If the game needs to go through a launcher before opening Nucleus will use this exe to start the game and it will still use the Game.ExecutableName process for positioning and resizing.

LauncherTitle.practice: While Nucleus looks for each instance's game window, a window whose title equals this (ignoring case) is treated as not the game yet, and Nucleus keeps looking. Use it for a launcher or splash window that shows up first under the game's process. Most handlers leave it empty; "splashscreen" is the usual value when there is one.

Play.doc: Called once per instance (player), in player order. By default it runs after Nucleus has set up the instance (Goldberg, XInput DLLs, ...) and before the game starts, and `Context.StartArguments` is read after it. `Game.GamePlayBeforeGameSetup` runs it before that setup; `Game.GamePlayAfterLaunch` runs it after the game has started (then `Context.StartArguments` has no effect). If both are true it never runs. `Context`, `Player`, `PlayerList`, `Handler` and `ProtoInput` are available inside it. An error thrown here ends the whole session.
Play.practice: Where nearly every handler does each instance's own setup: read `Context.Width`/`Height` and `Context.Nickname`, write configs with `Context.ModifySaveFile` or `Context.ReplaceLinesInTextFile`, copy files, and set `Context.StartArguments`.

SetupSse.doc: Never called by Nucleus (declared but unused): assigning it has no effect.

OnStop.doc: Called when the session ends, with the last player's `Context`/`Player`. If it throws, Nucleus skips its cleanup (leftover processes, registry restore, temporary users, backups), so keep it error-free. `Context` is undefined if the session ends before the first instance was set up.

OnFinishedSetup.doc: Called once after all instances have been set up and started, with the last player's `Context`/`Player`. An error thrown here ends the session.

HookFocus.practice: Nucleus injects its hooks into each instance after launch so the game is told it is the foreground window (GetForegroundWindow and the like), even when it isn't. True turns that check off, for games whose title changes (a version number, the level name, the FPS); handlers only set it when they need it, so it is nearly always true.

ResetWindows.doc: After each new instance opens, resize, reposition and remove borders of the previous instance.
ResetWindows.byEngine: By engine: rarer in Source games.
ResetWindows.practice: As each new instance starts, Nucleus puts the window of the one before it back to its place and size (and strips its borders again), for games that move or resize their window when another copy starts. Handlers that set it use true; it is especially common in Unity games.

PartialMutexSearch.doc: When killing handles, should a partial search be done with the handle name? | Renaming handles requires an exact match | default: false.

UseGoldberg.doc: Use the built-in Goldberg features in Nucleus | default: false.

It's the usual Steam emulation for Steam games across engines, nearly always together with `Game.SteamID`.

CopyCustomUtils.doc: Copy a file or folder you specify between the quotes to each instance folder, if the file/folder is located in Nucleus folder\utils\User. Use of parameters is separated by a | character. So it would look something like this [ "filename.ini|\\bin|1,2" ]. This example would copy filename.ini from Nucleus\utils\User to Instance0\bin and Instance1\bin. If you don't specify which instances, it will do them all by default. If you don't specify a path then root instance folder is used. If you want instances but root folder you would just do [ "filename.ini||1,2" ] | If copying multiple files, use comma seperated strings

CustomDllEnabled.doc: Use Nucleus' own XInput DLL (a custom x360ce) in each instance to give it one controller and keep it in focus. **On by default**: set it to `false` when the handler hands out controllers another way (XInputPlus with `Game.XInputPlusDll`, Proto Input), or Nucleus adds its DLL as well. `Game.Hook.XInputNames` says which DLL names it uses.

DInputEnabled.doc: If enabled, will allow DInput devices to be used as a device input in Nucleus. This doesn't mean that it will work with the game if not supported.
DInputEnabled.practice: True makes the setup screen list DirectInput controllers (as do `Game.Hook.XInputReroute` and `Game.ProtoInput.DinputDeviceHook`); with the custom XInput DLL it also goes into its settings. Only for the rare games that read controllers through DirectInput; almost every handler sets it false.

DInputForceDisable.doc: If we should completely remove support for DirectInput input from the game
DInputForceDisable.byEngine: By engine: more common in Source games, rarer in Unity games.

XInputEnabled.doc: If enabled, will allow XInput devices to be used as a device input in Nucleus. This doesn't mean that it will work with the game if not supported.
XInputEnabled.practice: Decides which controllers the setup screen lists: true lists XInput controllers (and hides their DInput twins); with `Game.Hook.CustomDllEnabled` it also goes into the custom DLL's settings. Proto Input's `Game.ProtoInput.XinputHook` lists them too. Set it true for games played with Xbox-style controllers; that's most handlers.

SDL2Enabled.doc: If the game supports sdl2 joysticks(not a hook)
SDL2Enabled.practice: Not a hook: Nucleus lists SDL2 controllers for the game and, for each instance, copies its own SDL2.dll (utils\SDL2\<arch>) next to the game's .exe, or into each folder in Game.SDLPaths, and writes SDL2.ini with that player's controller number. So it only works for games that load SDL2.dll as a separate file; a game with SDL built into its .exe (or a differently named SDL DLL such as SDL264.dll) keeps its own SDL and ignores it. Rare in Hub handlers; some also set Game.SDLPaths.

XInputNames.doc: Which XInput DLLs the custom DLL replaces. DInput DLLs are not supported.

XInputReroute.doc: If enabled, will allow XInput devices to act like DInput devices. This allows using more than 4 controllers. You can use only ONE XboxOne controller and you can't use at the same time the keyboard. You must click/alt+tab on the corresponding instance to make it work. In alternative, you can try to fix the problem by doing this [workaround](http://www.snes9x.com/phpbb3/viewtopic.php?t=27510) or try Xoutput.

ForceFocus.doc: If our custom x360ce xinput DLL should hook into the game's window and fake Window's events so we never leave focus.
ForceFocus.practice: It only goes into the custom XInput DLL's settings (ncoop.ini, ForceFocus), so it does nothing unless `Game.Hook.CustomDllEnabled` is true. Most handlers set it true without the custom DLL, where it changes nothing; focus is handled by Proto Input or the other focus options there.

ForceFocusWindowName.doc: If force focus is enabled, this is the window we are attaching ourselves to and the window we are going to keep on top. Needs the exact name of the window. If force focus is disabled you still need to set the game window name for resizing and positioning.
ForceFocusWindowName.practice: Even without the custom XInput DLL, Nucleus uses it to recognise each instance's game window: the window must have this title (within 2 letters, unless `Game.HasDynamicWindowTitle`), and processes are matched on their main window title. Put the exact title the game window shows; practically every handler sets it.

InjectStartup.doc: Nucleus starts each instance's game suspended, injects Proto Input, applies the `Game.ProtoInput` options and only then lets the game run, so the hooks are in place from its first line of code. This replaces Nucleus's other launch methods and the `InjectRuntime_…` options; it is not used with `Game.ThirdPartyLaunch` or `Game.NeedsSteamEmulation`. If injection fails, Nucleus shows an error and ends the session.

source.what: StartGame launch branch, runtime inject condition

InjectStartup.practice: For games that need the hooks before their first frame (raw input registered at startup, a launcher that checks focus), mostly Unreal Engine games; few handlers need it. It wins over the `InjectRuntime_…` options: Nucleus doesn't inject again at runtime when it is true.

source.what: if gen.ProtoInput.InjectStartup: ProtoInputLauncher.InjectStartup; the runtime branch needs !InjectStartup

InjectRuntime_RemoteLoadMethod.doc: Injects Proto Input into each instance's running game by making the game load the Proto Input DLL itself (a remote LoadLibrary call), once Nucleus has found its process, then applies the `Game.ProtoInput` options. Ignored when `Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup`, `Game.ProtoInput.InjectRuntime_EasyHookMethod` or `Game.ProtoInput.InjectRuntime_EasyHookStealthMethod` is on. If injection fails, Nucleus shows an error and ends the session.

InjectRuntime_EasyHookMethod.doc: Injects Proto Input with EasyHook into each instance's running game once Nucleus has found its process, then applies the `Game.ProtoInput` options. Ignored when `Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` is on, and `Game.ProtoInput.InjectRuntime_EasyHookStealthMethod` takes priority over it. If injection fails, Nucleus shows an error and ends the session.
InjectRuntime_EasyHookMethod.practice: The usual way handlers start Proto Input, for Unity and Unreal Engine games alike. Nucleus injects once it has found each instance's process, so the game's first moments run without the hooks; a game that registers raw input or checks focus right at startup needs `Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` instead (which then wins: the runtime injection is skipped).

source.what: InjectRuntime, Stealth, then EasyHook, then RemoteLoad

InjectRuntime_EasyHookStealthMethod.doc: Injects Proto Input into each instance's running game with EasyHook's stealth injection, once Nucleus has found its process, then applies the `Game.ProtoInput` options. When more than one runtime method is true, this one is used. Ignored when `Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` is on. If injection fails, Nucleus shows an error and ends the session.
InjectRuntime_EasyHookStealthMethod.practice: When several runtime methods are true, this one is used first (then EasyHook, then RemoteLoad). Few handlers need it; try it when a game notices or crashes on the normal EasyHook injection.

source.what: InjectRuntime, if easyHookStealthMethod ... else if easyHookMethod ... else if remoteLoadLibMethod

RegisterRawInputHook.doc: This hook will unsubscribe the game from Raw Input (if it has already subscribed to it), and then subscribes Proto Input to receive raw input instead. Raw input received is forwarded back to the game if it uses raw input. Proto Input receives all keyboard/mouse input from this hook so it always needs to be enabled.
RegisterRawInputHook.practice: This is the switch that makes Proto Input read each player's own keyboard and mouse: installing it is the only place Proto Input registers its raw input window, and it takes raw input away from the game (the game's own registrations are redirected to Proto Input). Everything per-player for keyboards and mice depends on it: the Send…Messages options post each player's input to their window, and the cursor and key state hooks (GetCursorPosHook, GetKeyStateHook, …) answer from the state it fills. Without it those hooks see no keys pressed and a frozen cursor. Most Proto Input handlers turn it on, many of them from Game.ProtoInput.OnInputLocked with ProtoInput.InstallHook.

source.what: (InstallImpl: FindAlreadySubscribedWindows, RawInput::UnregisterGameFromRawInput, RawInput::RegisterProtoForRawInput), RawInput.cpp (ProcessRawInput, Send…Messages), FakeMouseKeyboard

GetRawInputDataHook.doc: When forwarding the input back to the game, you need to create a handle to the input data. However these handles can only be created by Windows. To get around this, Proto Input will send a dummy WM_INPUT message to the game (from the Register Raw Input hook). The game then calls GetRawInputData using the dummy handle. This hook intercepts the call and passes in the saved data. This hook is required to make forwarding raw input work, so it should always be enabled.
GetRawInputDataHook.practice: Only matters for games that read raw input themselves. With Game.ProtoInput.RegisterRawInputHook on, Proto Input posts each player's raw input as WM_INPUT to the windows the game registered, tagged with its own signature; this hook lets the game's GetRawInputData read that data. Without the raw input hook it has nothing to pass on. Most Proto Input handlers turn it on, nearly always together with the raw input hook.

MessageFilterHook.doc: Hooks the GetMessage and PeekMessage functions to intercept every windows message for every window owned by the process. (Note this method is superior to changing WndProc since it works for all windows without knowing what they are, and is less fragile). This hook is used to make the message filters and blocks work. This should always be enabled.
MessageFilterHook.practice: The filters (`RawInputFilter`, `MouseButtonFilter`, ...) and `Game.ProtoInput.BlockedMessages` only act inside this hook, so they do nothing while it is off. Most Proto Input handlers turn it on, and many then enable the filters only while input is locked, from `Game.ProtoInput.OnInputLocked` with `ProtoInput.EnableMessageFilter`.

GetCursorPosHook.doc: The GetCursorPos is one way of obtaining the cursor position, so this hook redirects it to the "fake" cursor position. Should always be enabled.
GetCursorPosHook.practice: Answers the game's GetCursorPos with the player's own (fake) cursor position, kept by Proto Input from the raw input of the keyboard and mouse picked in Nucleus. That state is only filled while Game.ProtoInput.RegisterRawInputHook is on; without it the cursor seems frozen. It also answers from the controller when TranslateXinputtoMKB is on. Most Proto Input handlers turn it on, often from OnInputLocked, and nearly always with the raw input hook.

SetCursorPosHook.doc: SetCursorPos sets the cursor position. This hook causes it to set the "fake" cursor instead. This is important in some games that will set the mouse cursor to the centre of the screen each frame, then calculate the difference in movement each frame. This hook also prevents moving the "real" cursor, which can be problematic. Should always be enabled.

GetKeyStateHook.doc: Hooks GetKeyState to return the "fake" keyboard state. You should almost always have this enabled even if it appears to have no effect: when using multiple keyboards at the game time, they may interfere without this hook.
GetKeyStateHook.practice: Answers the game's GetKeyState with the player's own keys, kept by Proto Input from the raw input of the keyboard and mouse picked in Nucleus. That state is only filled while Game.ProtoInput.RegisterRawInputHook is on; without it the game sees no key pressed at all. Key hooks are used as a set: most Proto Input handlers turn on all three, often from OnInputLocked, and nearly always with the raw input hook.

GetAsyncKeyStateHook.doc: Similar to Get Key State. Async also tells the caller whether the key was pressed since the last call, so this can resolve issues where keys are pressed or release when they shouldn't. Should almost always be enabled.
GetAsyncKeyStateHook.practice: Answers the game's GetAsyncKeyState with the player's own keys, kept by Proto Input from the raw input of the keyboard and mouse picked in Nucleus. That state is only filled while Game.ProtoInput.RegisterRawInputHook is on; without it the game sees no key pressed at all. Key hooks are used as a set: most Proto Input handlers turn on all three, often from OnInputLocked, and nearly always with the raw input hook.

GetKeyboardStateHook.doc: Basically the same as Get Key State, except it returns the state of the entire keyboard. Should almost always be enabled.
GetKeyboardStateHook.practice: Answers the game's GetKeyboardState with the player's own keys, kept by Proto Input from the raw input of the keyboard and mouse picked in Nucleus. That state is only filled while Game.ProtoInput.RegisterRawInputHook is on; without it the game sees no key pressed at all. Key hooks are used as a set: most Proto Input handlers turn on all three, often from OnInputLocked, and nearly always with the raw input hook.

CursorVisibilityHook.doc: Monitors when the game tries to hide the cursor (e.g. when you close the menu in a first person game), and sets the visibility of the fake cursor instead. Should be almost always be enabled, except sometimes during debugging when you want to see where the fake mouse cursor is at all times. This hook also monitors calls to set the cursor image, so Proto Input will change the fake cursor to match the game's cursor image. Some games (notably Unity engine games) need DontShowCursorWhenImageUpdated enabled or the cursors will show when they shouldn't.

ClipCursorHook.doc: Prevents the game from setting a bounding region about the mouse cursor. Some games will repeatedly clip the cursor when they receive the fake focus, so this should almost always be enabled. Fake clip means that if the game tries to clip (i.e. bound) the real cursor, it will bound the fake cursor instead.

ClipCursorHookCreatesFakeClip.doc: Prevents the game from setting a bounding region about the mouse cursor. Some games will repeatedly clip the cursor when they receive the fake focus, so this should almost always be enabled. Fake clip means that if the game tries to clip (i.e. bound) the real cursor, it will bound the fake cursor instead.
ClipCursorHookCreatesFakeClip.byEngine: By engine: rarer in Source games.

FocusHooks.doc: Hooks many functions (see the Details tab of the hook) related to the game checking if it's in the foreground or focused. Should always be enabled. Proto Input will repeatedly scan to find the main window, in case it changes.
FocusHooks.practice: Hooks the functions a game uses to ask about focus (GetForegroundWindow, GetActiveWindow, GetFocus, WindowFromPoint, the capture and SetFocus calls), so every instance believes it is the active window. The most used Proto Input hook, nearly always on in Unreal Engine games; Unity games' handlers often do without it. Pair it with `Game.ProtoInput.BlockedMessages = [0x0008]` for games that also react to WM_KILLFOCUS, with `Game.ProtoInput.MessageFilterHook` on (the blocked messages only act inside that hook).

RenameHandlesHook.doc: Gives each instance its own copy of the named mutexes, events and semaphores listed in `Game.ProtoInput.RenameHandles` (and named pipes in `Game.ProtoInput.RenameNamedPipes`) by adding a random number to any name that contains a listed text, so instances don't detect each other. Only affects names the game creates or opens after Proto Input is injected. Needs `Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option.

XinputHook.doc: Xinput is used by most games for controller input. This hook changes the controller indexes so each instance can receive input from a different device. The controller index can be set from Nucleus or Proto Input Host, or it can be edited at runtime in the details tab. Xinput by default has a maximum of 4 controllers. This restriction can be removed if you enable use of the Openxinput library. However, this still will only let you use standard xinput controllers (no cheap PS1 controller adapters). If you want to use any device, enable the Dinput to Xinput redirection, which takes input from Direct Input (which supports any controller) and translates it to Xinput in the hook. Usually Openxinput is the best choice since it will work with vibration and using both triggers simultaneously.

DinputDeviceHook.doc:
Some (few) games will use Direct Input instead of Xinput to get controller input. The Direct Input API involves creating an "interface" to receive input from a controller. Typically a game will create this interface at startup for the first or all controllers. This hook will redirect the interface to the GUID of the selected controller. Note that the controller GUID can only be set automatically through Nucleus (not at runtime).
If this method doesn't work, you can also try with DinputHookAlsoHooksGetDeviceState. This will additionally hook the GetDeviceState function, which is called whenever the game polls input. This method is highly un-recommended since there's no guarantee the game expects the data to be formatted in the same way that Proto Input does, which can lead to completely mesesed up input.

SetWindowPosHook.doc: Prevents the game from calling SetWindowPos to resposition and resize the game window, instead forcing it to the resolution set by Nucleus. This will usually require using startup hooks.
SetWindowPosHook.byEngine: By engine: more common in Unreal Engine games.

BlockRawInputHook.doc: Blocks calls to GetRegisteredRawInputDevices and GetRawInputDeviceList to prevent the game from detecting raw input devices. You will usually need to use startup injection with this hook. If you enable this hook, you should **disable** the raw input filter, and add a block to WM_INPUT, like so: `Game.ProtoInput.BlockedMessages = [ 0x00FF ];`

FindWindowHook.doc: Blocks calls to FindWindow and EnumWindow so the game cannot detect any windows. This is required for opening multiple instances of some games. You will usually need to use startup injection with this hook.

CreateSingleHIDHook.doc: Hooks CreateFile so the game can only open the HID for the selected device (in Nucleus). This will usually require using startup injection.

SetWindowStyleHook.doc: Hooks SetWindowLong and SetWindowLongPtr to prevent the game from re-adding a title bar after Nucleus has stripped it.
SetWindowStyleHook.byEngine: By engine: more common in Unreal Engine games.

RawInputFilter.doc: Filters the WM_INPUT messages (which send raw input data) to only allow the forwarded messages from the Register Raw Input hook. This will allow only input from the selected device(s). Also modifies the message to tell the game that input was received while the game was in the foreground. Should always be enabled.
RawInputFilter.practice: Only acts inside `Game.ProtoInput.MessageFilterHook`. Handlers usually leave it false at the top and turn it on while input is locked instead: `ProtoInput.EnableMessageFilter(player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle, ProtoInput.Values.RawInputFilterID)` in `Game.ProtoInput.OnInputLocked` is the most common Proto Input call in Hub handlers.

MouseMoveFilter.doc: One method of getting the mouse position/state is through the WM_MOUSEMOVE message, so this modifies the data to return the "fake" mouse state. ****This filter is not recommended as it can be very CPU intensive (with multiple mice polling at hundreds of Hz), however it is required for input to work in some games.**** Test with it enabled and disabled to check if you require it.

MouseActivateFilter.doc: WM_MOUSEACTIVATE, WM_ACTIVATE and WM_ACTIVATEAPP all tell a window when it's activated or deactivated. These filters modify the messages to make the window think it's in the foreground and activated. Should always be enabled.

WindowActivateFilter.doc: WM_MOUSEACTIVATE, WM_ACTIVATE and WM_ACTIVATEAPP all tell a window when it's activated or deactivated. These filters modify the messages to make the window think it's in the foreground and activated. Should always be enabled.

WindowActvateAppFilter.doc: WM_MOUSEACTIVATE, WM_ACTIVATE and WM_ACTIVATEAPP all tell a window when it's activated or deactivated. These filters modify the messages to make the window think it's in the foreground and activated. Should always be enabled.

MouseWheelFilter.doc: Filters the WM_MOUSEWHEEL messages to only pass "fake" input. This fixes the issue of the foreground window receiving two scrolls for each scroll. Should always be enabled.

MouseButtonFilter.doc: Filters the mouse buttons messages to only pass "fake" input. This prevents any interaction from the "real" mouse cursor with our input. Should always be enabled.

KeyboardButtonFilter.doc: Same as the Mouse Buttons filter, for keyboard buttons. Should always be enabled.

BlockedMessages.doc: In the Block tab, you can select individual windows messages to block from the game. Usually a good one to block is WM_KILLFOCUS (0x0008). You can search for the hexadecimal code on MSDN, e.g. for [WM_KILLFOCUS](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/inputdev/wm-killfocus). Add the blocks to a handler like so:
BlockedMessages.practice: Window messages the game never sees (Proto Input's message filter hook drops them), so it only works with `Game.ProtoInput.MessageFilterHook` on; some handlers list messages without it. `[0x0008]` (WM_KILLFOCUS) keeps the game from noticing it lost focus, the usual list in Unreal Engine games; Unity games' handlers usually add WM_MOUSELEAVE and WM_MOUSEHOVER: `[0x0008, 0x02a3, 0x02a1]`. A number goes through Proto Input's own message table: one it doesn't list but within the table's range lands on another message's switch (and blocks that one), and one past its end does nothing, so add only listed messages.

RenameHandles.doc: Some games will use handles (of mutants, events or semaphores) or named pipes to prevent opening multiple instances. New instances will detect the handle opened by the previous instance, then refuse to open. Proto Input gets around this by renaming the handles to something random (e.g. "mutex" to "mutex2733894") so the new instances can't detect it. Since the handles are usually opened at startup, you will usually need startup injection. To get the names of these handles, use Process Explorer to browse the handles, then use some guesswork.

RenameNamedPipes.doc: Some games will use handles (of mutants, events or semaphores) or named pipes to prevent opening multiple instances. New instances will detect the handle opened by the previous instance, then refuse to open. Proto Input gets around this by renaming the handles to something random (e.g. "mutex" to "mutex2733894") so the new instances can't detect it. Since the handles are usually opened at startup, you will usually need startup injection. To get the names of these handles, use Process Explorer to browse the handles, then use some guesswork.
RenameNamedPipes.example: Game.ProtoInput.RenameNamedPipes = [ "some named pipe", "some other named pipe" ];

SendMouseWheelMessages.doc: Proto Input turns the player's mouse wheel into mouse wheel window messages sent to the game window. Applied per instance when Proto Input is injected (`Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option). Not sent while `Game.ProtoInput.TranslateMKBtoXinput` is on.

SendMouseButtonMessages.doc: Proto Input turns the player's mouse clicks (left, right, middle and the two side buttons) into button down/up window messages sent to the game window. Applied per instance when Proto Input is injected (`Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option). Ignored when `Game.ProtoInput.SendMouseDblClkMessages` is on (that option sends the clicks itself) or `Game.ProtoInput.TranslateMKBtoXinput` is on.

SendMouseMovementMessages.doc: Proto Input sends a mouse move window message with the player's fake cursor position to the game window each time the player's mouse moves. Applied per instance when Proto Input is injected (`Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option). Not sent while `Game.ProtoInput.TranslateMKBtoXinput` is on.
SendMouseMovementMessages.practice: Handlers turn the four Send…Messages options on together: games that read the mouse from window messages (WM_MOUSEMOVE and the like) then get each player's own mouse. Games that only read raw input don't need them.

SendMouseDblClkMessages.exampleNote: Generated from its type and default, not from the docs or Hub handlers.

EnableFocusMessageLoop.practice: Starts Proto Input's focus loop when Nucleus sets the instance up, with the `FocusLoop_…` messages and `FocusLoopIntervalMilliseconds`; those options do nothing without it. Many handlers leave it false and start the loop only while input is locked, with `ProtoInput.StartFocusMessageLoop` in `Game.ProtoInput.OnInputLocked`.

FocusLoopIntervalMilliseconds.doc: Milliseconds Proto Input's focus loop waits between rounds of focus messages to the game window. Default `5`. Only read when `Game.ProtoInput.EnableFocusMessageLoop` is on and Proto Input is injected (`Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option).
FocusLoopIntervalMilliseconds.byEngine: By engine: rarer in Source games.

FocusLoop_WM_ACTIVATE.doc: Proto Input's focus loop repeatedly tells the game window it was activated by a click (WM_ACTIVATE), so it believes it still has focus. Only read when `Game.ProtoInput.EnableFocusMessageLoop` is on and Proto Input is injected (`Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option).
FocusLoop_WM_ACTIVATE.byEngine: By engine: rarer in Source games.

FocusLoop_WM_ACTIVATEAPP.doc: Proto Input's focus loop repeatedly tells the game that its app became the active one (WM_ACTIVATEAPP), so it believes it still has focus. Only read when `Game.ProtoInput.EnableFocusMessageLoop` is on and Proto Input is injected (`Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option).
FocusLoop_WM_ACTIVATEAPP.byEngine: By engine: rarer in Source games.

FocusLoop_WM_NCACTIVATE.doc: Proto Input's focus loop repeatedly tells the game window to show itself as active (WM_NCACTIVATE), so it believes it still has focus. Only read when `Game.ProtoInput.EnableFocusMessageLoop` is on and Proto Input is injected (`Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option).
FocusLoop_WM_NCACTIVATE.byEngine: By engine: rarer in Source games.

FocusLoop_WM_SETFOCUS.doc: Proto Input's focus loop repeatedly tells the game window it has keyboard focus (WM_SETFOCUS). Only read when `Game.ProtoInput.EnableFocusMessageLoop` is on and Proto Input is injected (`Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option).

FocusLoop_WM_MOUSEACTIVATE.doc: Proto Input's focus loop repeatedly tells the game window it is being activated by the mouse (WM_MOUSEACTIVATE). Only read when `Game.ProtoInput.EnableFocusMessageLoop` is on and Proto Input is injected (`Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option).

DrawFakeCursor.doc: Enable this for games that don't have an in-game cursor

AllowFakeCursorOutOfBounds.doc:
If you want to allow the fake cursor to not be bound by the window boundaries, enable this

This can be useful as a workaround in some games that do not correctly reset the mouse cursor position to the window centre.

ExtendFakeCursorBounds.doc:
Some games may detect mouse input with an offset, in which case some regions of the window would be inaccessible since Proto Input bounds the fake cursor to the window by default.

You can get around this problem with this option: it will allow the fake cursor to go slightly beyond the window boundaries, so all regions should be accessible.

EnableToggleFakeCursorVisibilityShortcut.doc: Lets the player show or hide Proto Input's fake cursor with a key on their own keyboard (`Game.ProtoInput.ToggleFakeCursorVisibilityShortcutVkey`, Home by default); that key press is not passed to the game as a message. Needs `Game.ProtoInput.InjectStartup` or an `InjectRuntime_…` option.
EnableToggleFakeCursorVisibilityShortcut.byEngine: By engine: more common in Unity games, rarer in Source games.

DontShowCursorWhenImageUpdated.doc: Monitors when the game tries to hide the cursor (e.g. when you close the menu in a first person game), and sets the visibility of the fake cursor instead. Should be almost always be enabled, except sometimes during debugging when you want to see where the fake mouse cursor is at all times. This hook also monitors calls to set the cursor image, so Proto Input will change the fake cursor to match the game's cursor image. Some games (notably Unity engine games) need DontShowCursorWhenImageUpdated enabled or the cursors will show when they shouldn't.
DontShowCursorWhenImageUpdated.byEngine: By engine: more common in Unity games, rarer in Source games.

UseDinputRedirection.doc: Xinput is used by most games for controller input. This hook changes the controller indexes so each instance can receive input from a different device. The controller index can be set from Nucleus or Proto Input Host, or it can be edited at runtime in the details tab. Xinput by default has a maximum of 4 controllers. This restriction can be removed if you enable use of the Openxinput library. However, this still will only let you use standard xinput controllers (no cheap PS1 controller adapters). If you want to use any device, enable the Dinput to Xinput redirection, which takes input from Direct Input (which supports any controller) and translates it to Xinput in the hook. Usually Openxinput is the best choice since it will work with vibration and using both triggers simultaneously.

DinputHookAlsoHooksGetDeviceState.doc:
Some (few) games will use Direct Input instead of Xinput to get controller input. The Direct Input API involves creating an "interface" to receive input from a controller. Typically a game will create this interface at startup for the first or all controllers. This hook will redirect the interface to the GUID of the selected controller. Note that the controller GUID can only be set automatically through Nucleus (not at runtime).
If this method doesn't work, you can also try with DinputHookAlsoHooksGetDeviceState. This will additionally hook the GetDeviceState function, which is called whenever the game polls input. This method is highly un-recommended since there's no guarantee the game expects the data to be formatted in the same way that Proto Input does, which can lead to completely mesesed up input.

FreezeExternalInputWhenInputNotLocked.doc: This is identical to the setting in ProtoInputHost. You should leave this on so the "fake" input is only sent when the "real" input isn't

OnInputLocked.doc: Function Nucleus calls each time input is locked (the lock key, the gamepad lock shortcut or `Game.LockInputAtStart`), and once after all instances are set up if input is locked by then. It sees the last player's `Context`.
OnInputLocked.practice: Runs once when the player locks the input (the lock key, End by default), with no arguments, so handlers loop over `PlayerList` and act on each `player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle`. They use it to switch Proto Input on only while input is locked: `ProtoInput.InstallHook`, `ProtoInput.EnableMessageFilter`, `ProtoInput.SetDrawFakeCursor(…, true)`, `ProtoInput.StartFocusMessageLoop`, undone in `Game.ProtoInput.OnInputUnlocked`. `Context` in it is the last player's.

OnInputUnlocked.doc: Function Nucleus calls each time input is unlocked, once after all instances are set up if input is not locked by then, and when the session ends (before `Game.OnStop`). It sees the last player's `Context`.
OnInputUnlocked.practice: Runs once when the player unlocks the input, with no arguments (handlers loop over `PlayerList`). They undo here what `Game.ProtoInput.OnInputLocked` did: `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`, `ProtoInput.DisableMessageFilter`, `ProtoInput.SetDrawFakeCursor(…, false)`, so the real mouse works normally again.

AutoHideTaskbar.doc: Turns on the Windows taskbar's auto-hide when the session starts and turns it off again when the session ends. Does nothing if auto-hide was already on, or when `Game.HideTaskbar` hides the taskbar instead. Works without Proto Input being injected.

PatchFileFindPattern.doc: Reads `originalFile`, replaces every occurrence of the hex byte pattern `origPattern` (spaces allowed) and writes the result to `patchedFile`, even if nothing matched. Two forms: (`originalFile`, `patchedFile`, `origPattern`, `patchPattern`, `patchall`) puts the hex `patchPattern` in place of each match; (`originalFile`, `patchedFile`, `origPattern`, `insert`, `offset`, `patchall`) writes the low two bytes of the number `insert` (little-endian) into the pattern at one-based byte position `offset`. Throws if `originalFile` doesn't exist; returns true. In the first form, `patchall` false patches only the first byte of each match: pass true.

params.name: originalFile
params.doc: Full path of the file to read.

params.name: patchedFile
params.doc: Full path the patched bytes are written to; may be the same as originalFile.

params.name: origPattern
params.doc: Bytes to find as a hex string, spaces allowed, e.g. "8B 45 FC 89"; no wildcards.

params.name: patchPattern
params.doc: Replacement bytes as a hex string, at least as long as origPattern, written over each match byte by byte.

params.name: patchall
params.doc: With patchPattern: true patches every match fully, false only the first byte of each match. With insert: false stops after the first match.

params.name: originalFile

params.name: insert
params.doc: Number whose low two bytes (little-endian) are written into a copy of origPattern at offset, which then replaces the match.

params.name: offset
params.doc: Position in origPattern, counting bytes from 1, where the two insert bytes go.

params.name: patchall
params.doc: With patchPattern: true patches every match fully, false only the first byte of each match. With insert: false stops after the first match.

EditRegKey.doc:
Edit a registry key for current user, baseKey can either be "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE" or "HKEY_CURRENT_USER".
EditRegKey uses a custom registry data type to use, by using `Nucleus.RegType.DWord` for example. The last word can be of the same name of RegistryValueKind enum.

params.name: baseKey
params.doc: Registry root as text: "HKEY_CURRENT_USER", "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE" or "HKEY_USERS"; anything else and the call does nothing.

params.name: sKey
params.doc: Key path under the root, e.g. "Software\\Company\\Game"; created if missing. Before the first edit Nucleus exports it to utils\backup\<last part>.reg.

params.doc: Name of the value to set inside that key.

EditRegKey.byEngine: By engine: more common in Unity games, rarer in Source and Unreal Engine games.
EditRegKey.practice: Before it first changes a key, Nucleus exports it to utils\backup\<key>.reg, which it imports again afterwards (`Context.EditRegKeyNoBackup` skips that); a missing key is created. Only HKEY_CURRENT_USER, HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE and HKEY_USERS work; anything else, or a null value, is ignored without a word. Handlers use it in `Game.Play` for games that keep their resolution or window mode in the registry, which is mostly Unity games: they keep their screen settings in HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\<company>\<game>, and handlers set `Screenmanager Resolution Width` and `Height` there (the names end in a hash, `_h182942802`).

EditRegKeyNoBackup.doc: Edit a registry key for current user without Nucleus creating a backup of the registry or before it creates one. Must be placed before any "Context.EditRegKey" line in handler for it to work.

Hub.doc: Hub metadata. Written by hub.splitscreen.me when the handler is uploaded, and kept up to date there. Don't add or edit these lines yourself.

Maintainer.doc: The handler's uploader on hub.splitscreen.me, written by the Hub when the handler is uploaded. Nucleus doesn't read it.

Handler.doc: The handler's identity on hub.splitscreen.me. The Hub writes these lines when the handler is uploaded and again on every update; handler authors don't add or change them.

Name.doc: The uploader's name on hub.splitscreen.me, written by the Hub on upload. Nucleus doesn't read it.

Id.doc: The uploader's user ID on hub.splitscreen.me, written by the Hub on upload. Nucleus doesn't read it.

Version.doc: The published version number, written by the Hub on upload. With `Hub.Handler.Id`, Nucleus uses it to tell whether a newer version is on the Hub. Keep it as the Hub wrote it; the next upload sets the new number.

Id.doc: The handler's ID on hub.splitscreen.me, written by the Hub on upload. Nucleus uses it to link the installed handler to its Hub page: details, cover and screenshots, and update checks. Keep it exactly as the Hub wrote it, and don't copy it into another handler: a handler without it still works, it just isn't linked to the Hub.

LockInput.doc: Locks or unlocks the real mouse and keyboard for the whole PC (runs in Nucleus, not in a game): while locked, mouse input is blocked, keys are blanked and the cursor is clipped to the corner. Parameter: `true` to lock, `false` to unlock. Nucleus calls it itself when input is locked or unlocked; it returns the ID of its loop thread.

SuspendExplorer.doc: Suspends the threads of `explorer.exe` that own the taskbar, start menu, Alt+Tab and desktop menus, so they can't be opened by accident. `ProtoInput.RestartExplorer` must be called afterwards, or the desktop stays broken. Takes no parameters.

RestartExplorer.doc: Resumes the `explorer.exe` threads suspended by `ProtoInput.SuspendExplorer`. Takes no parameters. Nucleus calls it when input is unlocked.

RemoteLoadLibraryInjectRuntime.doc: Loads Proto Input into a running process by calling `LoadLibraryW` inside it. Parameters: the process ID and the folder that holds `ProtoInputHooks32.dll`/`ProtoInputHooks64.dll` (ending in a backslash). Returns the new instance handle, or 0 on failure.

EasyHookInjectRuntime.doc: Loads Proto Input into a running process with EasyHook, through the helper `ProtoInputIJ32.exe`/`ProtoInputIJ64.exe`. Parameters: the process ID and the folder that holds the Proto Input files (ending in a backslash). Returns the new instance handle, or 0 on failure.

EasyHookStealthInjectRuntime.doc: Same as `ProtoInput.EasyHookInjectRuntime`, but EasyHook injects in stealth mode (`EASYHOOK_INJECT_STEALTH`). Parameters: the process ID and the folder that holds the Proto Input files (ending in a backslash). Returns the new instance handle, or 0 on failure.

EasyHookInjectStartup.doc: Starts a game executable suspended and loads Proto Input into it before it runs. Parameters: the exe path, the command line, the process creation flags (Nucleus passes 0) and the folder that holds the Proto Input files. Returns the instance handle (0 on failure); the game stays suspended until `ProtoInput.WakeUpProcess`.

AddSelectedMouseHandle.doc: Assigns a mouse to the game instance, so its raw input drives that instance's fake mouse. Parameters: the instance handle and the mouse's raw input device handle. Can be called more than once to assign several mice.

AddSelectedKeyboardHandle.doc: Assigns a keyboard to the game instance, so its raw input drives that instance's fake keyboard. Parameters: the instance handle and the keyboard's raw input device handle. Can be called more than once to assign several keyboards.

SetTranslateXinputtoMKB.doc: When `true`, Proto Input turns the instance's controller into mouse and keyboard input for the game. It is switched off again if a mouse or keyboard was already assigned with `ProtoInput.AddSelectedMouseHandle` or `ProtoInput.AddSelectedKeyboardHandle`. Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`.

SetReregisterinput.doc: Option for the `RegisterRawInputHookID` hook: when `true` and the game registered for raw input without a target window, the game's main window gets the forwarded raw input. Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`. Set it before installing that hook, which reads it on install.

InstallHook.doc: Installs a Proto Input hook in the game instance. Parameters: the instance handle (`Player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle`) and a hook ID from `ProtoInput.Values` (the `...HookID` values). An unknown handle does nothing, and the call waits until Proto Input in the game has connected.

params.name: instanceHandle
params.doc: The player's Proto Input instance, Player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle (or PlayerList[i].ProtoInputInstanceHandle); Nucleus sets it when it injects Proto Input, otherwise it is 0.

params.name: hookID
params.doc: Which hook to install: a ProtoInput.Values.*HookID value, e.g. ProtoInput.Values.GetCursorPosHookID or ProtoInput.Values.FocusHooksHookID.

InstallHook.practice: Handlers call it in `Game.ProtoInput.OnInputLocked`, in a loop over `PlayerList`, so a hook acts only while input is locked, and remove it again with `ProtoInput.UninstallHook` in `Game.ProtoInput.OnInputUnlocked`. The cursor and key state hooks are the usual ones: GetCursorPosHookID, SetCursorPosHookID, GetKeyStateHookID, GetAsyncKeyStateHookID, GetKeyboardStateHookID.

UninstallHook.doc: Removes a Proto Input hook from the game instance. Parameters: the instance handle (`Player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle`) and a hook ID from `ProtoInput.Values` (the `...HookID` values).

params.name: instanceHandle
params.doc: The player's Proto Input instance, Player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle (or PlayerList[i].ProtoInputInstanceHandle).

params.name: hookID
params.doc: Which hook to remove: a ProtoInput.Values.*HookID value, the same one passed to InstallHook.

EnableMessageFilter.doc: Turns on a window message filter in the game instance. Parameters: the instance handle (`Player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle`) and a filter ID from `ProtoInput.Values` (the `...FilterID` values). Filters only act while the `MessageFilterHookID` hook is installed.

params.name: instanceHandle
params.doc: The player's Proto Input instance, Player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle (or PlayerList[i].ProtoInputInstanceHandle).

params.name: filterID
params.doc: Which filter to turn on: a ProtoInput.Values.*FilterID value, e.g. ProtoInput.Values.RawInputFilterID or ProtoInput.Values.WindowActivateFilterID.

EnableMessageFilter.practice: Turns a message filter on for one instance. It only acts with `Game.ProtoInput.MessageFilterHook` on. Handlers call it in `Game.ProtoInput.OnInputLocked` and the matching `ProtoInput.DisableMessageFilter` in `Game.ProtoInput.OnInputUnlocked`; RawInputFilterID and MouseButtonFilterID are the common filters.

DisableMessageFilter.doc: Turns off a window message filter in the game instance. Parameters: the instance handle (`Player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle`) and a filter ID from `ProtoInput.Values` (the `...FilterID` values).

params.name: instanceHandle
params.doc: The player's Proto Input instance, Player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle (or PlayerList[i].ProtoInputInstanceHandle).

params.name: filterID
params.doc: Which filter to turn off: a ProtoInput.Values.*FilterID value, the same one passed to EnableMessageFilter.

EnableMessageBlock.doc: Blocks a window message in the game instance: the game reads it as an empty message (`WM_NULL`). Parameters: the instance handle (`Player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle`) and the message number. Only acts while the `MessageFilterHookID` hook is installed, and the number goes through Proto Input's own message table, so an unlisted number can block a different message.

DisableMessageBlock.doc: Stops blocking a window message that `ProtoInput.EnableMessageBlock` blocked. Parameters: the instance handle (`Player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle`) and the message number.

WakeUpProcess.doc: Resumes the threads of a game started suspended by `ProtoInput.EasyHookInjectStartup`, then looks for its main window again. Parameter: the instance handle. Nucleus calls it after setting up hooks and options.

UpdateMainWindowHandle.doc: Sets which window Proto Input treats as the game's main window (focus, cursor and input messages target it). Parameters: the instance handle and the window handle; 0 makes Proto Input pick the first visible top-level window of the game itself. After a non-zero handle, Proto Input stops searching for the main window on its own.

SetupState.doc: Tells Proto Input in the game which instance number it is, starting at 1 (lower values are refused). Parameters: the instance handle and the number. Proto Input uses it for its window shortcut (right Ctrl + right Alt + that number key opens its GUI) and shows it there.

SetupMessagesToSend.doc: Chooses which window messages Proto Input posts to the game window from the assigned mouse and keyboard. Parameters, in order: the instance handle, then `true`/`false` for mouse wheel, mouse button, mouse move, keyboard key and mouse double-click messages.

StartFocusMessageLoop.doc: Starts posting focus messages to the game's main window in a loop, so the game believes it is focused. Parameters, in order: the instance handle, the interval in milliseconds, then `true`/`false` for `WM_ACTIVATE`, `WM_ACTIVATEAPP`, `WM_NCACTIVATE`, `WM_SETFOCUS` and `WM_MOUSEACTIVATE`.

params.name: instanceHandle
params.doc: The player's Proto Input instance, Player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle (or PlayerList[i].ProtoInputInstanceHandle).

params.name: milliseconds
params.doc: Pause between rounds of fake focus messages, in milliseconds.

params.name: wm_activate
params.doc: true posts WM_ACTIVATE (click-activate) to the game window each round.

params.name: wm_activateapp
params.doc: true posts WM_ACTIVATEAPP (activated) to the game window each round.

params.name: wm_ncactivate
params.doc: true posts WM_NCACTIVATE (active title bar) to the game window each round.

params.name: wm_setfocus
params.doc: true posts WM_SETFOCUS to the game window each round.

params.name: wm_mouseactivate
params.doc: true posts WM_MOUSEACTIVATE to the game window each round.

StartFocusMessageLoop.practice: Starts Proto Input's focus loop for one instance from a callback, instead of `Game.ProtoInput.EnableFocusMessageLoop` at setup. The arguments are the instance, the milliseconds between rounds, then whether to send WM_ACTIVATE, WM_NCACTIVATE, WM_ACTIVATEAPP, WM_SETFOCUS and WM_MOUSEACTIVATE. Handlers mostly call it in `Game.ProtoInput.OnInputLocked`, often right after `ProtoInput.StopFocusMessageLoop`.

StopFocusMessageLoop.doc: Pauses the focus message loop started by `ProtoInput.StartFocusMessageLoop`. Parameter: the instance handle.

params.name: instanceHandle
params.doc: The player's Proto Input instance, Player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle (or PlayerList[i].ProtoInputInstanceHandle).

SetDrawFakeCursor.doc: Shows or hides the fake cursor Proto Input draws over the game for this instance. Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`.

params.name: instanceHandle
params.doc: The player's Proto Input instance, Player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle (or PlayerList[i].ProtoInputInstanceHandle).

params.name: enable
params.doc: true draws Proto Input's fake mouse cursor in that instance, false hides it.

SetDrawFakeCursor.practice: Shows or hides Proto Input's fake cursor in one instance, for games that have no cursor of their own. Handlers show it in `Game.ProtoInput.OnInputLocked` (with true); some hide it again in `Game.ProtoInput.OnInputUnlocked` (with false).

SetDrawFakeCursorFix.doc: Switches the fake cursor to an alternative drawing mode that offsets it by the cursor image's detected hotspot and does not resize it for the monitor scale. It does not turn drawing on: `ProtoInput.SetDrawFakeCursor` does. Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`.

SetExternalFreezeFakeInput.doc: When `true`, Proto Input stops passing the assigned mouse and keyboard input to the game instance. Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`. Nucleus sets it to `true` while input is not locked when the freeze-external-input option is on.

SetControllerIndex.doc: Chooses the controllers the game instance sees through the `XinputHookID` hook. Parameters: the instance handle, then the controller for the game's XInput slots 1 to 4, counted from 1; 0 means no controller in that slot. With `ProtoInput.SetTranslateXinputtoMKB` on, the first controller is translated to mouse and keyboard and every slot reports no controller.

SetUseDinputRedirection.doc: When `true`, the `XinputHookID` hook reads a DirectInput controller (the one chosen by `ProtoInput.SetControllerIndex`, among DirectInput devices) and gives it to the game as an XInput controller. Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`. Call it before installing the `XinputHookID` hook.

source.what: comment: must be called before InstallHook on the Xinput hook

SetUseOpenXinput.doc: When `true`, the `XinputHookID` hook reads controllers through OpenXinput instead of `xinput1_3.dll`, which allows controller numbers above 4. Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`.

SetTranslateMKBtoXinput.doc: When `true`, the `XinputHookID` hook presents the instance's mouse and keyboard as an XInput controller in the slots that have no controller. Meanwhile the key state hooks report no keys pressed and raw input is not forwarded to the game. Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`.

SetShowCursorWhenImageUpdated.doc: Option for the `CursorVisibilityStateHookID` hook. When `true`, every `SetCursor` call with a cursor image shows the fake cursor; when `false`, `SetCursor` only hides it (on a null cursor). Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`.

SetPutMouseInsideWindow.doc: When `true`, the fake cursor is kept inside the game window (from 0 to width minus 1) and its drawing window is placed with the game window instead of covering every screen. Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`.

SetDefaultTopLeftMouseBounds.doc: With `ProtoInput.SetPutMouseInsideWindow` on, `true` restores the default top and left limit of the fake cursor (-1 instead of 0). Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`.

SetDefaultBottomRightMouseBounds.doc: With `ProtoInput.SetPutMouseInsideWindow` on, `true` restores the default bottom and right limit of the fake cursor (the window width and height instead of one pixel less). Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`.

SetDontWaitWindowBorder.doc: Option for the `RemoveBorderHookID` hook: when `true`, it removes the main window's border right away on install instead of waiting up to 10 seconds for the window to get one. Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`. Set it before installing that hook.

AddHandleToRename.doc: Needs the `RenameHandlesHookID` hook. Any mutex, event or semaphore the game creates or opens whose name contains this text gets a random number appended, so instances don't see each other's. Parameters: the instance handle and the text (up to 998 characters).

AddNamedPipeToRename.doc: Needs the `RenameHandlesHookID` hook. Any named pipe the game creates whose name contains this text gets a random number appended. Parameters: the instance handle and the text (up to 998 characters).

SetDinputDeviceGUID.doc: Chooses the DirectInput controller the `DinputOrderHookID` hook opens for every DirectInput device the game creates. Parameters: the instance handle and the controller's GUID (Nucleus passes `player.GamepadGuid`); a second form takes the GUID as 11 numbers (Data1, Data2, Data3, then the 8 bytes of Data4).

SetDinputHookAlsoHooksGetDeviceState.doc: When `true`, the `DinputOrderHookID` hook also hooks the controller's `GetDeviceState`. Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`. Call it before installing the `DinputOrderHookID` hook.

source.what: comment: must be called before InstallHook on the Dinput order hook

SetSetWindowPosSettings.doc: Sets the position and size the `SetWindowPosHookID` hook applies to every `SetWindowPos` call. Parameters: the instance handle, x, y, width, height (Nucleus passes the player's screen area).

SetSetWindowPosDontResize.doc: When `true`, the `SetWindowPosHookID` hook keeps the size the game asked for and only forces the position. Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`.

SetSetWindowPosDontReposition.doc: When `true`, the `SetWindowPosHookID` hook keeps the position the game asked for and only forces the size. Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`.

SetCreateSingleHIDName.doc: Sets the one HID device path the `CreateSingleHIDHookID` hook lets the game open; opening any other path containing "HID" or "hid" fails. Parameters: the instance handle and the device path (Nucleus passes `player.RawHID`).

SetCursorClipOptions.doc: Option for the `ClipCursorHookID` hook. `true` (the default) turns the game's `ClipCursor` area into a limit for the fake cursor; `false` ignores the game's `ClipCursor` calls. Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`.

SetToggleFakeCursorVisibilityShortcut.doc: Sets a key that shows or hides the fake cursor when pressed on the instance's keyboard; that key press is not passed to the game. Parameters: the instance handle, `true`/`false` to enable the shortcut, and the virtual-key code.

AllowFakeCursorOutOfBounds.doc: Changes how far the fake cursor can move. Parameters: the instance handle, `allowOutOfBounds` (`true`: no limit at all) and `extendBounds` (`true`: the limits reach past the window edges, by 100 pixels or, with `ProtoInput.SetPutMouseInsideWindow`, to twice the window size).

SetRawInputBypass.doc: When `true`, raw input from every mouse and keyboard is forwarded to the game unchanged, not only from the assigned devices, and Proto Input's fake mouse and keyboard are not updated from it. Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`.

params.name: instanceHandle
params.doc: The player's Proto Input instance, Player.ProtoInputInstanceHandle (or PlayerList[i].ProtoInputInstanceHandle).

params.name: enable
params.doc: true passes raw input from every device to the game, not just the player's; false lets Proto Input filter it per device.

SetPointerInMouse.doc: When `true`, Proto Input subclasses the game's main window and turns mouse messages into pointer messages (`WM_POINTERUPDATE`, `WM_POINTERDOWN`, `WM_POINTERUP`, `WM_POINTERWHEEL`) for games that read pointer input. Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`.

SetSendMessagesToSubWindows.doc: When `true`, left, middle and right mouse button messages are also posted to the child window under the fake cursor, not only to the main window. Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`.

GetTaskbarAutohide.doc: Returns `true` if the Windows taskbar is set to auto-hide. Takes no parameters.

SetTaskbarAutohide.doc: Turns auto-hide of the Windows taskbar on (`true`) or off (`false`). It also turns the taskbar's always-on-top state off.

SetMoveWindowSettings.doc: Sets the position and size the `MoveWindowHookID` hook applies to every `MoveWindow` call. Parameters: the instance handle, x, y, width, height (Nucleus passes the player's screen area).

SetMoveWindowDontResize.doc: When `true`, the `MoveWindowHookID` hook keeps the size the game asked for and only forces the position. Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`.

SetMoveWindowDontReposition.doc: When `true`, the `MoveWindowHookID` hook keeps the position the game asked for and only forces the size. Parameters: the instance handle and `true`/`false`.

SetAdjustWindowRectSettings.doc: Sets the rectangle the `AdjustWindowRectHookID` hook starts from: every `AdjustWindowRect`/`AdjustWindowRectEx` call computes the window size from this position and size, without a menu. Parameters: the instance handle, x, y, width, height (Nucleus passes the player's screen area).

SetManualScaling.doc: Rescales the mouse position the game sees (mouse messages, `GetCursorPos`, `GetCursorInfo`) by `oldX`/`newX` and `oldY`/`newY`. Parameters: the instance handle, then `oldX`, `oldY`, `newX`, `newY`; it is ignored unless all four are above 5. Nucleus passes the handler's scale-from size and the player's screen size.

SetXinputtoMKBkeys.doc: Sets the controller-to-keyboard mapping used by `ProtoInput.SetTranslateXinputtoMKB`. Parameters, in order: the instance handle; virtual-key codes for A, B, X, Y, right shoulder, left shoulder, D-pad right, left, up, down, right stick press, left stick press, stick right, left, up, down, Back and Start; then sensitivity, acceleration and deadzone.

SetXinputtoMKBCFG.doc: Sets options for `ProtoInput.SetTranslateXinputtoMKB`. Parameters, in order: the instance handle; swap sticks; screen scanning (moves the cursor to points found from .bmp images or static points); shoulder buttons jump to the next point; then for A, B, X and Y in turn: static point, click, move.

Values.doc: Hook and message filter IDs for `InstallHook`, `EnableMessageFilter`, ...

RegisterRawInputHookID.doc: Selects the RegisterRawInput hook (ID 0): the game's `RegisterRawInputDevices` calls no longer reach Windows, and Proto Input forwards only the assigned mouse and keyboard's raw input to the game's windows. Pair it with `GetRawInputDataHookID`, which decodes the forwarded input. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
RegisterRawInputHookID.exampleNote: Generated from its type and default, not from the docs or Hub handlers.

GetRawInputDataHookID.doc: Selects the GetRawInputData hook (ID 1): when the game reads raw input that Proto Input forwarded, it gets the assigned device's data; other raw input passes through unchanged. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
GetRawInputDataHookID.exampleNote: Generated from its type and default, not from the docs or Hub handlers.

MessageFilterHookID.doc: Selects the message filter hook (ID 2) on `GetMessage`/`PeekMessage`: messages the game reads carry the fake cursor position, and the enabled filters and blocked messages apply. The `...FilterID` filters and `ProtoInput.EnableMessageBlock` only work while it is installed. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
MessageFilterHookID.exampleNote: Generated from its type and default, not from the docs or Hub handlers.

GetCursorPosHookID.doc: Selects the GetCursorPos hook (ID 3): gives each instance its own cursor position, as `GetCursorPos` returns the instance's fake cursor. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
GetCursorPosHookID.exampleNote: Generated from its type and default, not from the docs or Hub handlers.

SetCursorPosHookID.doc: Selects the SetCursorPos hook (ID 4): the game's `SetCursorPos` moves only the instance's fake cursor, not the real one. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
SetCursorPosHookID.exampleNote: Generated from its type and default, not from the docs or Hub handlers.

GetKeyStateHookID.doc: Selects the GetKeyState hook (ID 5): `GetKeyState` reports the keys and buttons of the instance's assigned keyboard and mouse. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
GetKeyStateHookID.exampleNote: Generated from its type and default, not from the docs or Hub handlers.

GetAsyncKeyStateHookID.doc: Selects the GetAsyncKeyState hook (ID 6): `GetAsyncKeyState` reports the keys and buttons of the instance's assigned keyboard and mouse. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
GetAsyncKeyStateHookID.exampleNote: Generated from its type and default, not from the docs or Hub handlers.

GetKeyboardStateHookID.doc: Selects the GetKeyboardState hook (ID 7): `GetKeyboardState` reports the keys and buttons of the instance's assigned keyboard and mouse. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
GetKeyboardStateHookID.exampleNote: Generated from its type and default, not from the docs or Hub handlers.

CursorVisibilityStateHookID.doc: Selects the cursor visibility hook (ID 8): the game's `ShowCursor`, `SetCursor` and `SetSystemCursor` calls show, hide and set the image of the instance's fake cursor. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
CursorVisibilityStateHookID.exampleNote: Generated from its type and default, not from the docs or Hub handlers.

ClipCursorHookID.doc: Selects the ClipCursor hook (ID 9): the game's `ClipCursor` no longer confines the real cursor; by default it confines the fake cursor instead (see `ProtoInput.SetCursorClipOptions`). Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
ClipCursorHookID.exampleNote: Generated from its type and default, not from the docs or Hub handlers.

FocusHooksHookID.doc: Selects the focus hooks (ID 10): `GetForegroundWindow`, `GetActiveWindow`, `GetFocus`, `GetCapture` and `WindowFromPoint` return the game's main window, and `SetFocus`, `SetForegroundWindow` and similar calls do nothing, so the game believes it always has focus. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
FocusHooksHookID.byEngine: By engine: more common in Source games.
FocusHooksHookID.exampleNote: Generated from its type and default, not from the docs or Hub handlers.

RenameHandlesHookID.doc: Selects the rename handles hook (ID 11): mutexes, events, semaphores and named pipes whose names match `ProtoInput.AddHandleToRename` or `ProtoInput.AddNamedPipeToRename` get a unique name, so instances don't block each other. Pass it to `ProtoInput.InstallHook` or `ProtoInput.UninstallHook`.
